titolo: Kaggle's free GPU for AI models: what you get, step by step, with real numbers
descr: Two free T4 cards, 29 GB of RAM and 30 hours a week. How to run Qwen3.8-27B on Kaggle with Ollama, how fast it is, and the limits and rules to read first.
paragrafi: Kaggle lends you two graphics cards for free. With the T4 x2 option you get two NVIDIA T4 cards, 4 CPU cores and 29 GB of RAM, for about 30 hours a week and up to 12 hours per session. That is enough to run a 27-billion-parameter model with no card of your own.

Videos call this a 32 GB server, but our session showed about 15 GB per card, and the memory sits on two separate cards. Ollama loads a model on one GPU if it fits, and spreads it across both if it does not. Qwen3.8-27B is too big for one card, so it split, with about 9 GB on each and 100 percent on the GPU.

The steps are short. Create a notebook, choose GPU T4 x2 and turn Internet on. Install Ollama with the official command, start it in the background, then pull qwen3.8:27b-q4_K_M, an 18 GB download with an Apache 2.0 license. Run it with the verbose option to read the speed.

We ran the same test on both machines. On Kaggle the model wrote about 13 tokens per second, so an answer of 256 tokens takes about 20 seconds. A home RX 7900 XTX with 24 GB wrote between 50 and 66. Check that the GPUs are working with ollama ps and nvidia-smi, and press Stop Session when you finish, because an open session keeps using your hours.

You can reach the notebook from your PC with a tunnel, but a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel is public, and it is meant for testing and development. Anyone with the address can use your model unless you add a password. Avoid connecting a coding agent that can run commands on your computer.
perche: Read the rules before you build on this. Kaggle's policy lists server farming and activity unrelated to machine learning among the abuses of its resources. A few hours of model tests fit. A free API for your daily work puts your account at risk. If your own card has enough memory, running at home has no quota at all.
